SMTO-JOB-0004 — SMTO can't safely stop the job that's in the way

GUID: 91928748-9847-45bf-8137-828359af30c1
Slug: resource-stop-not-eligible
Domain: JOB · Subsystem: job

What happened

  • Your command hasn't started because another job is using what it needs. SMTO can't stop that job for you because it can't confirm the job's program is still running under its watch.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In the Job recovery card, select Wait until the job state changes. SMTO continues on its own as soon as the other job releases what your command needs.
  2. Check the computer that job runs on to see whether its program is still running. SMTO can't confirm that program's state, so the computer itself shows whether the job is really still busy.
  3. If you're sure the job's work isn't needed and the card offers Resolve forcefully by terminating job, use it. That option ends the blocking job through a separate, checked path and frees what it was using.

What success looks like

  • The Job recovery card goes away and your command starts.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the Gateway. Don't end programs on that computer unless you're sure they belong to this job.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A correlated stop-blockers request was refused because at least one blocking job is not cancel-eligible (its running process identity or supervisor cannot be confirmed).

What this means

  • A correlated stop-blockers request finds at least one current resource blocker whose cancel_eligible flag is false. Job identity, supervision and dispatch/terminal receipts own effect truth. Diagnostics do not launch, cancel or replay work; missing output or failed control does not prove that the original process stopped.

Why this can happen

  • A correlated stop-blockers request finds at least one current resource blocker whose cancel_eligible flag is false.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect every exact blocker and its current cancellation eligibility; no stop is committed for this rejected group.

How to fix it

  • GatewayJobs._commit_blocker_control returned resource_stop_not_eligible: a blocker lacks a confirmed command_pid and process identity, is not running, or its supervisor is not alive. Inspect the blocker's job state on the Gateway and use wait, reconciliation or the reviewed reset path instead of unsupported termination.
  • Inspect the actual job or terminal state and use an available control action.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • A supported eligible control acts on known owners, or the blocking state is reconciled without unsupported termination.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Job identity, supervision and dispatch/terminal receipts own effect truth. Diagnostics do not launch, cancel or replay work; missing output or failed control does not prove that the original process stopped.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
